accuracy_findings.claim: Buildings on moons and asteroids have no such cap. Each of their levels from level 2 needs a patent, the same one for all of them.
accuracy_findings.problem: The most natural reading of "the same one for all of them" is one patent for all of their levels, and that is wrong. Each level needs a different patent (levels 2 to 5 each have their own). Every building on a moon or asteroid shares the patent for a given level. Having the level 2 patent does not let you order level 3. Readers who skip the table get the wrong rule.
accuracy_findings.fix: Say that each level has its own patent and that all moon and asteroid buildings share it. For example: "From level 2, each level needs its own patent, the same one for every building on a moon or asteroid." This matches the brief's "one shared patent per level".

clarity_findings.claim: "Buildings on moons and asteroids have no such cap. Each of their levels from level 2 needs a patent, the same one for all of them."
clarity_findings.problem: "the same one for all of them" most naturally binds to the nearest plural noun, "levels" — reading as if one single patent covers every level from 2 to 5. The actual rule (borne out by {table:upgrade_patents}, which lists a distinct patent per level) is that all orbital buildings share one patent AT a given level, and each level has its own. A player skimming this sentence could come away with the wrong mental model of the mechanic itself, not just a style nit.
clarity_findings.fix: Re-anchor "the same one" to the buildings, not the levels, e.g.: "Buildings on moons and asteroids have no such cap. From level 2 up, each level needs its own patent, shared by every building there."

clarity_findings.claim: "That infrastructure level counts only once its own upgrade is finished."
clarity_findings.problem: The pronoun chain ("That infrastructure level ... its own upgrade") sits right after a sentence about the OTHER buildings' level cap, so a reader has to backtrack to confirm this clause is about the infrastructure building's upgrade, not the other building's. A brief stumble, not a wrong reading once re-read.
clarity_findings.fix: Name the subject directly instead of leaving it to a pronoun, e.g.: "The infrastructure building's new level counts toward that cap only once its own upgrade is finished."

accuracy_findings.claim: In a Flash game, every building has one level, so nothing can be upgraded. ... For example: {name:building.infra_open} at level 3: the other buildings on that planet can reach level 3 / {table:upgrade_patents}

Below the example sits a lone 'None' paragraph, which is what the empty table prints. That output is correct (Flash has no upgrade patents), but with no lead-in a Flash reader cannot tell what 'None' refers to. The page has had this since round 0. You could also move the Flash sentence to the end of 'What each level needs', straight after the table. Then a Flash reader sees 'None' followed by the reason, and does not first read that nothing can be upgraded and then meet a level 3 example.
